Subject: Dedicated capacity pilot & MAP draft (BlueHorizon)

Hi Logan —

Thanks again for the demo last week. As we discussed, BlueHorizon is ready to run a focused evaluation of dedicated capacity for our high-throughput inference pipeline (customer-support reranking + multi-turn chat). We need a short mutual plan and an initial pricing strawman so our procurement and infra teams can scope approvals.

High-level asks:
- Pilot size: estimate for 80-120 GPU-equivalent pool (we currently use ~3K tokens/sec peak) — please confirm sizing assumptions.
- Evaluation window: 4–6 weeks preferred.
- Pricing: reserved commit for pilot, plus clear burst behavior during ramp. We need to understand how bursts are billed and any caps.
- MAP: milestones tied to evaluation metrics (latency, error rate, cost/unit) and a path-to-commit if we hit targets.

I've attached an internal MAP draft (BH_MAP_v3.pdf) and a rough GPU sizing worksheet (GPU_Sizing_Sheet.xlsx). Procurement is looped (procurement@bluehorizon.ai) — they'll need billing cadence, PO instructions, and SOW before we start.

Can you share a short milestone-linked pricing proposal by EOD Monday so we can review with procurement? Also open to a quick call Monday afternoon.

Best,
Elena
VP Product, BlueHorizon AI

Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity pilot & MAP draft (BlueHorizon)

Elena — thanks for the clear asks and the attachments. I ran the sizing worksheet with our infra team and sketched an evaluation-first commercial structure that ties MAP milestones to committed capacity and discounts. Summary below; I'll attach a one-page pricing sheet (RDW_Eval_Pricing_v2.pdf) for procurement.

Proposal (pilot-first):
- Pilot pool: 100 A100-equivalent vGPU units (config: 80 active slots + 20 warm/kv-cache nodes) — this matches the token throughput you shared with ~20% buffer.
- Eval window: 6 weeks (2-week warm/ramp, 4-week measurement).
- Two commercial paths (pick at pilot close):
  1) 12-month reserved commit: baseline rate $X per vGPU-hour (net of discount) with an 18% volume discount; guaranteed minimum monthly commit = 60% of pilot pool for first 3 months, then flexible step-ups.
  2) 6-month reserved (shorter term): 10% discount, higher overage multiplier.
- Burst clause (we want this to be predictable):
  - Allowed burst: up to 50% of committed pool for the first 30 days of go-live, then reduced to 30% unless you elect an alternative burst bucket.
  - Billing for burst: first 30% of burst usage covered by a monthly "burst credit" that builds with your commit (credits = commit * 0.08); additional burst billed at 1.5x baseline vGPU-hour rate. Alternatively, you can purchase a capped burst bucket (prebought credits) at a lower blended rate.
- MAP milestones (example):
  Wk0–Wk2: infra onboarding + KV cache tuning (success = <12% p99 tail relative to baseline)
  Wk2–Wk6: workload validation (success = stable latency and <2% quality regression on eval set)
  At pilot close: option to sign reserved commit path with agreed discount and start date.

Commercial notes:
- Billing cadence: monthly in arrears; PO required before reserved start for enterprise commit path.
- Security docs: SOC2 report and network diagram available on request.

I'll be on a short call Mon 15:00 PT if you'd like to walk this through. I attached RDW_Eval_Pricing_v2.pdf with the numbers and a sample SOW outline.

Cheers,
Logan
Head of Sales — East
Redwood Inference

Hi Elena / procurement team —

Quick procurement note from Redwood ops to get the pilot lined up: 
- Billing: monthly in arrears based on committed vGPU-hours + measured burst overage. We support hourly granularity with minute-level metering; rounding >1 minute is prorated.
- Preemption: reserved pools are non-preemptible. Any transient worker VMs we spin for burst are billed as on-demand and marked explicitly in the invoice.
- KV-cache nodes: included in the vGPU-hour rate as long as they are part of the reserved pool; separate managed KV tiers available for dedicated caching at additional cost (we noted your worksheet has them included).
- PO instructions: see attached PO_Instructions.docx — please raise PO to RedWood, Inc. (billing@redwood.ai) and include deal id RDW-2026-BH-37.

I'll also include a short SOW template if helpful; Logan has the commercial terms. Let me know procurement contact and we can schedule a quick onboarding packet review.

Thanks,

2) Burst safety: cap billable burst at 50% of committed pool for first 90 days (we'll provide a spillover credit method in writing).

We should hold firm on the 18% discount for the 12-month term. Get procurement the PO instructions and SOW; if they accept the credit & burst cap, prepare an A/R timeline and DocuSign-ready SOW/contract.
